header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Karen Lee (Aurora - Dir. Data Science), Rajiv Malhotra (Aurora - Head of ML), Tom O'Neal (Aurora - Platform Eng)
summary: Redwood demo focused on Eval & Quality Monitoring (Prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons). Customer is evaluating options for production monitoring of model regressions for claims automation and policy Q&A. Key asks: integration with existing prompt sets, alerting thresholds tied to business metrics, A/B traffic split support for rollouts, and private deployment considerations. Agreed next steps: share pricing/pilot, security docs, and run technical benchmarks with Aurora's prompts.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. we ll keep this to about 45 minutes, demo the eval and quality monitoring flow and then leave time for Qs.
[00:12] Karen: Thanks Samira, excited to see this. quick context - we're automating first-pass claims triage and policy Q&A, we had some weird regressions when we moved models last quarter so monitoring is a big must for us.
[00:25] Diego: Totally, sounds familiar. Today we'll show prompt set management, how to wire up regression alerts, and A/B compare surfaces in the console plus the API for automation.
[00:38] Rajiv: Couple of asks up front - can alerts be tied to business metrics (like Mispred rates or escalation rate) and is there an SLA for the monitoring service?
[00:50] Samira: Good question. monitoring ties to your eval metrics, you can map eval signals to business KPIs via our console and webhook integrations; SLA varies by plan but Dedicated has uptime backed SLAs. I'll follow up with exact numbers in the security deck.
[01:05] Tom: for private deployments we need KMS/HSM support and audit logs retained for 7 years, is that supported?
[01:15] Diego: yes we have KMS integrations and long-term audit retention as an add-on for Private. I'll include the doc link after the call.
[01:25] -- screen share starts --
[01:30] Diego: Ok showing the Redwood Console. first panel is Prompt Sets - you can group prompts by intent, tag golden prompts for regression checks, and set sampling rates for production comparison.
[01:45] Diego: here's an example 'claims triage' prompt set - we store historical outputs and attach eval labels so you can compute quality over time. note the transcription here is auto-ingested, so sometimes field names get mangled (we can map keys).
[02:05] Karen: can we import our existing prompt spreadsheet? we have about 2k prompts.
[02:12] Diego: yes CSV import, also API to push prompt sets. large imports support chunking and there's a preview step to fix common OCR/name mismatches.
[02:25] Diego: next, regression alerts - you create a baseline (either golden prompts or rolling baseline). set thresholds (absolute delta or percent) and configure channels: Slack, PagerDuty, email, webhook.
[02:40] Samira: we recommend a hybrid: golden prompts for semantic correctness and cohort baselines for overall distribution drift.
[02:50] Rajiv: how do you handle model variant mismatches? e.g., floating point quantized vs fp16 affect tokenization and scores.
[02:58] Diego: great point. we support model variant tagging in the eval. when you run A/B, the system normalizes metrics where possible and flags mismatches; for kernel/quantization differences we include a model artifact fingerprint so you can filter comparisons. sometimes you need manual review for edge cases.
[03:20] -- timestamp jump --
[03:30] Diego: demoing A/B compare: you can route a percentage of traffic to a candidate and run side-by-side metrics on accuracy, hallucination score, latency, cost per 1k tokens. here's a saved A/B we ran internally comparing quantized-llama variant vs fp16.
[03:50] Karen: can the A/B tie into our rollouts? we use feature flags and would like automatic ramp up on metric success.
[03:58] Diego: yes, our rollouts support manual and automatic policies — e.g., auto ramp to 50% if key metric delta is within tolerance for X hours. You can also set automatic fallback if latency or error rate spikes.
[04:16] Rajiv: what about statistical significance? we need p-values or confidence intervals before we change production models.
[04:25] Diego: built in. A/B reports include confidence intervals, sample sizes, and Bayesian estimates if you prefer.
[04:35] Samira: i'll note that in the next steps, Diego will share the A/B config template so you can tweak priors.
[04:44] -- customer interruptions / cross talk --
[04:50] Karen: latency budget for claims path is 250ms 95th, how do batching and caching affect that with larger seq lengths?
[04:59] Diego: Auto batching tries to keep within your SLO by trading off some throughput. prefix/KV caching reduces repeated prefix cost - for chat flows it's huge. we surfaced token-level latency breakouts in the console so you can see where time is spent. quantization can reduce cost but may slightly change accuracy — Optimize recommends safe quant profiles per workload.
[05:25] Tom: Do you have a suggested config for seq len ~512 with typical claim text ~200 tokens?
[05:33] Diego: yes, we'll share Optimize recommendations: suggested batch size, KV cache TTLs, and quant profiles. For 200 tokens most customers hit good latency at batch size 8 with realtime SLOs.
[05:45] -- switch to API demo --
[05:50] Diego: API endpoints for eval are simple: submit prompt set, annotate examples, create baseline, and watch regression alerts. here's an example curl to push a prompt and expected label. note tokenization differences can cause off by one errors in exact match metrics, we have token alignment helpers in SDK.
[06:15] Rajiv: is there SDK support for python and go?
[06:20] Diego: yep python, node, go. we also have sample notebooks for eval pipelines.
[06:28] Karen: what about retention - do you keep user content? we have privacy constraints and PII to scrub.
[06:35] Samira: retention policies are configurable by workspace; for Private you control retention and redaction. for Hosted we offer configurable retention windows and PII scrubbing helpers.
[06:48] -- format issues in transcript --
[06:50] Speaker 1: uh so if a prompt is golden but the output changes slightly, will that fire an alert?
[06:58] Diego: you can set tolerance - exact match for strict, semantic similarity thresholds otherwise. we have an embedding-based similarity score and heuristics for paraphrase detection.
[07:10] Rajiv: can human labels be used to retrain or to bias the scoring?
[07:16] Diego: yes annotations feed back into eval metrics; you can tag an example as "accepted" or "rejected" and use that for downstream A/B weighting or to trigger reweighting.
[07:28] -- mid demo notes --
[07:30] Diego: showing alerts UI - you can include example diffs and stack traces, link back to the request id, and open a ticket automatically.
[07:44] Karen: we'd like alerts to include business context e.g., "increase in manual escalations" - can you add custom payloads to webhooks?
[07:52] Diego: yes custom webhook payloads, and you can map eval metrics to custom KPIs via our API.
[08:03] Tom: any thoughts on storing golden prompts in our Git repo vs console? we want code review and PRs for prompt changes.
[08:12] Samira: good practice is to store canonical prompts in your repo and use CI to push changes to Redwood via the API; we have a GitHub Action sample that automates push and tagging.
[08:23] -- small glitch, audio lag --
[08:30] Speaker 2: ok uh moving on to reporting - history views show trend lines and ability to pivot by model version.
[08:40] Diego: here's an example regression alert that fired when we rolled a new model - you can see per-prompt diffs and a summary delta.
[08:50] Rajiv: How easy is it to backfill historical data for older model versions? we have logs going back a year.
[08:58] Diego: backfill supported via API or bulk import; we recommend chunked import and include a migration checklist. performance of backfill depends on size but it's straightforward.
[09:10] Karen: on A/B comparisons, can we run pairwise comparisons across more than two variants?
[09:18] Diego: yes multi-arm comparisons are supported but we recommend pairwise for clarity; multi-arm will give you adjusted p-values and ranking.
[09:28] -- tension, quick objection --
[09:30] Rajiv: cost - we are sensitive to per-token monitoring costs. how do you minimize cost for massive volume?
[09:36] Samira: Optimize suggests sampling, caching, and delta checks - you don't need to store every token. also dedicated pools reduce per-token compute cost and batching helps. we'll include estimated cost models in the pilot proposal.
[09:50] Karen: if we do a pilot, can we run it against production traffic or a sampled copy?
[09:58] Diego: both. you can sample traffic live or replay logs. we support traffic mirroring to a private cluster if you want zero impact on prod.
[10:10] -- final Qs --
[10:15] Tom: do you have prebuilt templates for insurance use cases (claims, underwriting)?
[10:22] Diego: yes we have industry prompt templates and eval suites; we'll share the insurance pack.
[10:30] Karen: timing - we're aiming to pick a vendor by end of October.
[10:35] Samira: understood, that aligns with a Sept pilot and October decision.
[10:42] -- recap and next steps --
[10:45] Samira: quick recap: we'll send pilot proposal + pricing, Diego will share benchmark config and the GitHub Action sample, and Aurora will send sample prompts and success criteria. we'll schedule the technical deep dive for week of 9/15.
[10:58] Rajiv: great, thanks!
[11:00] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday.
[11:05] -- call ends --
